nodes.characterization_summary: Ir species in Ir₁/NOC disperse exclusively as single atoms anchored on the support surface without nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM (AC-HAADF-STEM) images unequivocally demonstrate that the Ir species disperse exclusively as single atoms anchored on the support surface without the presence of nanoparticles (Figures 1a and S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: HREELS of Ir₁/NOC displays characteristic signals from N, O, and C species around the Ir₁ center.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the high-resolution electron energy loss spectrum (HREELS) of Ir₁/NOC displays characteristic signals from both N and O species in conjunction with C species (Figure 1a and Figure S6a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f_{7/2} binding energy of Ir₁/NOC is 62.50 eV consistent with Ir(IV) oxidation state; N 1s deconvolution reveals Ir-N peak at 399.8 eV; Ir NPs/AC shows 61.71 eV approaching metallic Ir and lacks Ir-N peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1c and Table S2, the Ir 4f_{7/2} binding energy for Ir₁/NOC is 62.50 eV, consistent with the Ir(IV) oxidation state.[36,37] In contrast, the corresponding binding energy for Ir NPs/AC is 61.71 eV, approaching the metallic Ir. Deconvolution of the N 1s spectrum for Ir₁/NOC (Figure 1d) reveals five distinct nitrogen species: pyridinic N (398.5 eV), Ir-N (399.8 eV), pyrrolic N (400.7 eV), graphitic N (401.5 eV), and oxidized N (403.0 eV).[25] In contrast, Ir NPs/AC lacks the Ir-N peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir₁/NOC EXAFS shows dominant peak at 1.52 Å attributed to Ir-O/N coordination; quantitative fitting yields coordination number 2.1 for Ir-O and 2.37 for Ir-N confirming Ir-O₂N₂ configuration; no Ir-Ir (2.71 Å) or Ir-O-Ir (3.15 Å) peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS spectrum of Ir₁/NOC displays a dominant peak at 1.52 Å (Figure 1e), attributed to Ir-O/N coordination... Quantitative EXAFS fitting (Figure 1f and Table S4) yields an average coordination number of 2.1 for Ir-O and 2.37 for Ir-N, suggesting that the first-shell coordination environment of Ir in Ir₁/NOC adopts an Ir-O₂N₂ configuration.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES white-line peak of Ir₁/NOC higher than Ir foil, approaching IrO₂, confirming oxidized Ir state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES spectrum (Figure S8) reveals that the white-line peak of Ir₁/NOC is higher than that of Ir foil while it approaches IrO₂, demonstrating the oxidized state of Ir.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows only graphitic carbon (002) and (100) peaks, no detectable metallic Ir or IrO₂ reflections.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis reveals two characteristic graphitic carbon peaks on the above catalysts corresponding to the (002) and (100) planes, with no detectable reflections from metallic Ir or IrO₂ species (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Both Ir₁/NOC and Ir NPs/AC exhibit block-shaped morphologies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show that both Ir₁/NOC and Ir NPs/AC samples predominantly exhibit block-shaped morphologies (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping confirms coexistence of Ir, N, and O throughout Ir₁/NOC sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This result is further verified by the larger scale energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping (Figure S6b) and elemental analysis techniques (Table S3), which confirm the coexistence of Ir, N, and O elements throughout the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform analysis shows Ir₁/NOC with lobe at (~1.5 Å, 4.7 Å⁻¹) corresponding to Ir-O/N coordination; Ir foil shows characteristic Ir-Ir bonding lobe at (~2.7 Å, 11.2 Å⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further confirmation is provided by wavelet transform (WT) analysis (Figure 1h). The Ir foil displays a characteristic WT lobe at (~2.7 Å, 11.2 Å⁻¹), indicative of Ir-Ir metallic bonding, while Ir₁/NOC exhibits a distinct lobe at (~1.5 Å, 4.7 Å⁻¹), corresponding to Ir-O/N coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRF detects 0.2 wt% Cl species in Ir₁/AC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (XRF) detects the presence of 0.2 wt% Cl species
